hook.line: Don Hernando has been coming to the café since 1979, and he loves to tell you how it was back then. To describe a place or a person in the past, Spanish has a second kind of past, made for painting the picture.
hook.es: En 1979 el café era pequeño y Rosa tenía treinta años.
hook.en: In 1979 the café was small and Rosa was thirty.

examples.es: Había una radio en la pared.
examples.en: There was a radio on the wall.

What was Rosa like?
She had a real temper.

rule:
English has one *was* for everything. Spanish keeps a special past for describing: what something was like, where it was, how old someone was, what there was. It paints the background, with no start or finish in view.

*ser*: *era*, *eras*, *era*, *éramos*, *eran*
*estar*: *estaba*, *estabas*, *estaba*, *estábamos*, *estaban*
*tener*: *tenía*, *tenías*, *tenía*, *teníamos*, *tenían*
*hay* becomes *había*: there was, there were. One form for both.

Notice that I and he or she are the same here: *era* can be I was or she was. Add *yo* or a name when it matters.

Compare *fue*: *El sábado fue un desastre* sums up an event. *El café era pequeño* describes how it looked. For describing, use *era*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the imperfect (*pretérito imperfecto*). Here you meet it with the describing verbs only; the rest of it comes later.
soundTip: The stress sits early: *Era* is EH-rah, *tenía* is teh-NEE-ah, *estaba* is es-TAH-bah. In *estábamos* and *éramos* the stress jumps back a syllable, which is why they carry an accent mark.

options: Rosa is going to be thirty.

readAndPick.es: Había una radio en la pared.
options: There was a radio on the wall.
There is a radio on the wall.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: *El café ___ pequeño.* (*es* or *era*) The café was small.
yourTurn.why: It's a description of the past, so *era*.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: *Rosa ___ treinta años.* (*fue* or *tenía*) Rosa was thirty.
yourTurn.why: Age uses *tener*, even in the past: *tenía*.

yourTurn.prompt: There was a radio on the wall.
yourTurn.answer: Había una radio en la pared.
accept: En la pared había una radio.

yourTurn.prompt: We were tired. (a group of men, or a mixed group)
yourTurn.why: How you felt uses *estar*: *estábamos*, with the accent mark.
What someone was is *era*, and no *un* before the job.
*Hay* becomes *había*, and it stays the same for many things.
We were is *éramos*, and the adjective goes plural too.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask Don Hernando, politely: How old were you in 1979?
yourTurn.why: With *usted*, use the he and she form: *tenía*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. In Spanish you have your years, so age is always *tener*: *tenía*.
Close. *Había* stays the same for one thing or many, just like *hay*.
Nearly. The we form carries an accent mark: *estábamos*, *éramos*.
*Fue* sums up an event. For what a place was like, Spanish uses *era*.

personal: Think of a house or a street from your childhood. Write three sentences: what it was like (*era*), what there was (*había*) and how old you were (*tenía*).
